Senses.Explanation: Receiving emptiness and answering an echo is responding to what has no substance of one’s own. Chan speakers apply the paired image to inherited talk and imitative responses, often immediately contrasting it with a present demand or blow. Yinyuan Longqi contrasts empty reception with working the local ground; Chaozong applies it to inherited talk; Tianyin Xiu warns the echo-following person not to move; Baiyu Jingsi applies the phrase to Kasyapa in the flower-sermon case; and Lianyue forbids it while raising the whisk.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB171.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Tianyin. Tianyin Yuanxiu lifts his whisk before the assembly and personally declares that the preceding old adepts are pierced by his whisk and thrown before his listeners.

Senses.Explanation: To pierce through the nostrils is to catch someone so completely that the person can be led by the nose. Chan speakers make a staff, whisk, or verbal dilemma perform the piercing, marking mastery over every position the other party might take. Chulin Shangrui says Xinghua’s staff pierces even a traveler who claims not-west and returns east. Huiyue Xu raises Tianyi Huai’s staff piercing both buddha and demon, then disputes the appraisal. Yichu Wuyuan says speaking and not speaking are equally pierced. Tianyin Yuanxiu says his whisk pierces the nostrils of the old masters he has just raised.

Senses.Explanation: The “meaning from the West” is the shortened public-interview form of the question about the patriarch’s coming from the West; the records answer it with fresh words and actions rather than one explanatory definition. Direct abbreviated questions ask simply “what is the meaning from the West?” Tianzhu Chonghui answers with a white ape carrying its young and butterflies holding flowers; Helin Xuansu answers that understanding is not understanding and doubt is not doubt. Yunfeng Zudeng answers with striking the forehead and nose, an unnamed monk asks Mazu Daoyi and Mazu answers “what meaning is present now?”, Sanfeng Hanyue Fazang says “three years carrying one boat,” Longya asks Linji and Linji demands the Chan board, Zhaozhou descends from the seat, and Shitou sends the questioner to ask the exposed pillar. The Chan bend is the abbreviation’s life as a public test whose many incompatible replies are preserved rather than harmonized into a hidden proposition.

Senses.Explanation: Xihe playing with the lion names the characteristic lion handling associated with Fenyang Shanzhao of Xihe. Sanyi Mingyu places it among old masters' displays and sets it before the line about one punch killing Cen the Tiger. Yunwai Xingze cries the phrase after asking who remains outside his all-encompassing birthday scene. In two image encomia, Shaweng Huihai calls Xihe's lion play the house of the founding ancestor and pairs it with Linji's staff and shout.
